deed: ז'ורז' שרפק, ניצול מחנה הריכוז דכאו, המציא את גלאי החלקיקים הרב-חוטי וזכה בפרס נובל
title: Georges Charpak, a Dachau survivor, invented a multiwire particle detector and won the Nobel Prize

trailer.text: Georges Charpak was a particle physicist who worked at CERN in Geneva from 1959 to 1991, and won the Nobel Prize for his invention and development of a particle detector.
Georges Charpak was born to Jewish parents, and his family left Poland and settled in Paris in 1932.
After the German occupation he joined the French Resistance, was arrested and sent to the Dachau concentration camp.
In 1968, while working at CERN, he developed the multiwire proportional chamber, a more effective way of detecting particles.
The device made it possible to record up to one million particle tracks per second, and devices based on it detected the W and Z particles and the top quark.

stations.title: A child from a Jewish shtetl

paragraphs.text: Charpak was born to Jewish parents, Chana (Szapiro) and Maurice Charpak.
He recounted that the family was mainly Jewish and spoke Yiddish, like all the residents of the shtetl.
According to him, Jews made up three quarters of the town's residents, and the conditions imposed on them were difficult.
In 1932 his parents and his younger brother left Poland and settled in Paris.
Georges came to France with his parents when he was seven years old.
After the German occupation in 1940 the family was caught up in the persecution of Jews.
The family members refused to wear the yellow star and lived under false names.
Charpak warned his cousin.
The family left Paris with forged papers in the name of Charpentier.
On 15 February 1943 Charpak joined the Resistance movement Francs-Tireurs et Partisans.
He organized a rebellion of soldiers in a youth camp and distributed leaflets against the Vichy government and against forced labor conscription.
On 10 August 1943 the French police arrested him in Montpellier.
On 23 December 1943 he was sentenced to a fine of 2000 francs and two years in prison for communist activity.
In the Montpellier prison he took part in a revolt of prisoners who refused the transfer of two of them to Germany.
In the Eysses central prison he taught his fellow prisoners physics and mathematics.
On 19 February 1944 he took part in a collective escape attempt, in order to join the Resistance fighters.
The escape failed, and on 23 February 1944 12 men were executed.
On 30 May 1944 Charpak was handed over to the German authorities, who took him to Compiègne.
On 20 June 1944 he arrived at Dachau and was registered there under the number 73251.
In the Landsberg subcamp the prisoners built a runway for jet aircraft with shovels and pickaxes.
During the death march Charpak was chosen to dig the burial pits for the dead.
On 30 April 1945 he was liberated at Allach.
Charpak wrote that physics filled his memory and helped him keep at bay what he chose to bury.

stations.title: Back to life and to physics

paragraphs.text: Only when he returned from deportation did Charpak learn that he had been admitted to the École des Mines.
In 1946 he became a French citizen.
He married Dominique Vidal.
According to Wikipedia, they had three children.
In 1959 he began working at CERN in Geneva and switched his focus to high-energy particle physics.
In 1961 his group demonstrated that the muon is only a heavy cousin of the electron.
As energies increased, analyzing the photographs from the bubble chamber became more and more tedious.
At first it was often the wives of the doctoral students who examined the photographs in search of rare events.
Charpak decided to build a new type of detector.
It was a gas detector, inspired by the Geiger-Müller tube.
In 1968 he developed the multiwire proportional chamber.
The chamber contains many parallel metal wires, surrounded by a gas.
When particles enter the chamber, electrons in the gas are liberated in a cascade, and currents are generated in the wires that are registered and processed by computers.
Charpak installed several rows of wires in planes at different angles and connected them directly to computers.
In his Nobel Prize acceptance speech Charpak said that his contribution was the art of weaving in space thin wires that detect charged particles produced in high-energy nuclear collisions.
The multiwire chamber was patented and quickly superseded the old bubble chambers.
The multiwire chamber achieved a counting rate up to a thousand times higher than existing detectors such as the bubble chamber.
Instead of just a few, it was now possible to record up to one million particle tracks per second.
According to Physics World, it increased the data collection speed by a factor of 1000 compared with previous techniques.
Researchers began working with much higher collision rates.
According to CERN Courier, the invention took particle physics into the electronic age.
According to the Swedish Academy's citation, thanks to his work particle physicists were able to focus on very rare interactions.
Devices based on the multiwire chamber detected the W and Z particles at CERN and the top quark at Fermilab.
According to Futura-Sciences, without Charpak's invention it would have been impossible to discover the W and Z bosons.
CERN Director-General Rolf Heuer said that without Charpak's methods, above all the multiwire chamber, the LHC program would to a large extent be impossible today.
According to Times Higher Education, Charpak was among those responsible for the development of the Large Hadron Collider.
The detector has applications in medicine, biology and industry.
One of his notable successes in medicine is the EOS system, which displays all the bones of the skeleton in three dimensions from two low-dose X-ray images.
According to the obituary in Physics World, he also developed a radon detector that could help predict earthquakes.
Charpak was awarded the Nobel Prize for his invention and development of particle detectors, in particular the multiwire proportional chamber.
With the prize, the Swedish Academy recognized not only his contribution to science but also his contribution to society.
On 13 October 1992 a blind hadron detector was demonstrated at CERN, the day before his award was announced.
On 20 May 1985 he was elected to the French Academy of Sciences.
In 1989 he received the High Energy Particle Physics Prize of the European Physical Society.
In 1999 he received the Golden Plate Award of the American Academy of Achievement.
In Saint-Genis-Pouilly, near CERN, there is a street named after him.
In 1972 Charpak, together with Daniele Amati, launched a petition against the Vietnam War.
In 1978 he canceled his participation in a congress in Dubna, Soviet Union, in protest against the imprisonment of physicist Yuri Orlov.
Charpak loved popularizing science, and wrote several books to make physics accessible to the general public.
He was one of the founders of 'Hands in the Dough' (La main à la pâte), an Academy of Sciences initiative for teaching science in primary school, launched in 1995.
In 1996 he started a program to train primary school teachers in France to teach hands-on science.
After his mother's death he decided to invest in preserving the Brens camp.
In 1991 he retired from CERN.
He died on 29 September 2010 in Paris.
The authors of the Physics Today obituary described him as a great humanist, enthusiastic, creative, open-minded and thoughtful.

claims.quote: After Georges went to work at CERN in Geneva in 1959, he switched his scientific interest to high-energy particle physics.

claims.text: שרפק סיפר שהמשפחה הייתה יהודית בעיקרה ודיברה יידיש כמו כל תושבי סרני, העיירה שבה נולד בפועל לדבריו.
claims.quote: Nous étions surtout juifs et nous parlions yiddish comme tous les gens de Sarny, le Shtetl où je suis réellement né

claims.quote: Le 15 juillet 1942 Jean Demarq, dont le père est policier, prévient Georges qu’une rafle est prévue le 16 juillet 1942

claims.quote: Dans la nuit du 20 au 21 décembre il participe à la prison de Montpellier à la révolte des prisonniers qui refusent le départ de deux d’entre eux pour l’Allemagne.

claims.text: בכלא המרכזי של אייס לימד שרפק את חבריו פיזיקה ומתמטיקה.
claims.quote: Georges Charpak dispense des cours de physique et mathématiques à ses compagnons.

claims.quote: Il participe le 19 février 1944 à la tentative d’évasion collective afin de rejoindre les maquis.

claims.quote: Il est remis le 30 mai 1944 aux autorités allemandes qui le conduisent à Compiègne.

claims.text: שרפק הגיע לדכאו ב-20 ביוני 1944 ונרשם שם תחת המספר 73251.
claims.quote: il arrive au camp de concentration nazi de Dachau le 20 juin 1944, il y est enregistré sous le matricule 73251.

claims.text: במחנה המשנה לנדסברג בנו האסירים מסלול המראה למטוסי סילון בעזרת את ומכוש.
claims.quote: Les déportés y construisent, avec pelles et pioches, une piste d’envol pour les avions à réaction.

claims.quote: Georges Charpak est désigné pour creuser les fosses pour les morts.

claims.quote: La physique à fort opportunément rempli ma mémoire, tenant en respect ce que j’ai préféré enfouir.

claims.quote: Ce n’est qu’à son retour de déportation qu’il apprend qu’il est admis.

claims.text: שרפק הפך לאזרח צרפתי ב-1946, והוריו היגרו לצרפת כשהיה בן 7.
claims.quote: Georges Charpak était devenu citoyen français en 1946 (ses parents ont immigré en France quand il avait 7 ans)

claims.quote: Dans les premiers temps, ce seront souvent les femmes des doctorants qui auront pour tâche d'examiner ces photos à la recherche d'événements rares.

claims.quote: In 1999, Charpak received the Golden Plate Award of the American Academy of Achievement.

claims.text: בסן-ז'ניס-פואיי שליד CERN יש רחוב על שמו.
claims.quote: there is a street named in his honor

claims.text: ב-1972 יזם שרפק יחד עם דניאלה עמאטי עצומה נגד מלחמת וייטנאם.
claims.quote: in 1972, together with Daniele Amati, he launched a petition against the Vietnam War.

claims.text: ב-1978 ביטל שרפק את השתתפותו בכנס בדובנה בברית המועצות במחאה על מאסרו של הפיזיקאי יורי אורלוב.
claims.quote: in 1978 Georges canceled his participation in a congress in Dubna, Soviet Union, to protest the imprisonment of physicist Yuri Orlov.

claims.text: שרפק היה נלהב מהפצת המדע וכתב כמה ספרים כדי להנגיש את הפיזיקה לקהל הרחב.
claims.quote: He was passionate about popularizing science, and he wrote several books to make physics accessible to the general public.

claims.text: שרפק היה ממיזמי 'ידיים בבצק' (La main à la pâte) שהושקה ב-1995 בידי האקדמיה למדעים לקידום הוראת המדעים בבית הספר היסודי.
claims.quote: lancée en 1995 par l’Académie des sciences. Cette opération a pour but de promouvoir l’enseignement des sciences à l’école primaire.

claims.text: ב-1996 יזם שרפק תוכנית להכשרת מורים בבתי ספר יסודיים בצרפת להוראת מדע מעשית.
claims.quote: In 1996 Georges started a program that trains primary school teachers in bringing hands-on science to students in France.

claims.text: לאחר מות אמו החליט שרפק להשקיע בשימור מחנה ברן.
claims.quote: décide de s’investir dans la préservation du camp de Brens

claims.text: שרפק מת ב-29 בספטמבר 2010 בפריז.
claims.quote: He died on 29 September 2010 in Paris.

claims.text: מחברי ההספד בפיזיקס טודיי תיארו אותו כהומניסט דגול, נלהב, יצירתי, פתוח וחושב.
claims.quote: We will fondly remember this great humanist who was highly enthusiastic, creative, open minded, and thoughtful.

claims.text: לפי ויקיפדיה, שרפק נולד ב-1 באוגוסט 1924 בדומברוביצה שבפולין.
claims.quote: (1924-08-01)1 August 1924 Dąbrowica, Wołyń Voivodeship, Second Polish Republic

claims.text: לפי גיליון ביוגרפי צרפתי, שרפק נולד רשמית ב-1 באוגוסט 1924 בדומברוביצה שבפולין.
claims.quote: Georges, Hersz Charpak est né officiellement le 01 aout 1924 à Dabrovica en Pologne.

claims.text: לפי ההספד בפיזיקס טודיי, שרפק נולד בדומברוביצה שבפולין ב-8 במרץ 1924, ובשנת 1932 עברה משפחתו לפריז.
claims.quote: Georges was born in Dabrovica, Poland, on 8 March 1924, and in 1932 he and his family moved to Paris.

claims.text: לפי נאום שנשא שרפק שנה קודם, הוא נולד ב-8 במרץ 1924, אף שהתאריך תועד עד אז כ-1 באוגוסט.
claims.quote: According to a speech he gave last year, Georges Charpak was born in the Polish village of Dabrovica, now in the Ukraine, on 8 March 1924

claims.text: לפי הגיליון הביוגרפי, שרפק עצמו מציין שנולד ב-8 במרץ 1924.
claims.quote: Georges Charpak indique être né le 08 mars 1924.

claims.text: לפי פיזיקס טודיי, שרפק קיבל דוקטורט בפיזיקה גרעינית ב-1954.
claims.quote: where he earned his PhD in nuclear physics in 1954

claims.text: לפי האנציקלופדיה היהודית, שרפק קיבל דוקטורט ב-1955 מהקולג' דה פרנס.
claims.quote: He received a Ph.D. in 1955 from the College de France, Paris
